summary: Child of ATTEMPT-LAMBDA7-FIRST-MOVER-PURE-ACT (#352): source the two bare bridges of ARIST-MET-XII-7-FIRST-MOVER-PURE-ACT so that the Lambda.7 route to STMT-FIRST-UNMOVED-MOVER-IS-PURE-ACT ties or beats the ST I q.3 a.1 route and the root no longer needs act's simple priority. Witnesses newly pinned and read whole: Met. V.5 (ARIST-MET-V-5) and XII.9 (ARIST-MET-XII-9), Perseus Greek, same snapshot as XII.7; Aquinas, In Metaph. V, lect. 6 (AQUINAS-IN-METAPH-V-L6, Corpus Thomisticum web snapshot, new manifest) and XII, lect. 11 (AQUINAS-IN-METAPH-XII-L11, same snapshot as lect. 7); XII.7 1072b4-30, IX.8 1050b6-19 and lect. 7 n. 12-16 re-read. Findings. (1) Can-fail bridge, sourced. Met. V.5, 1015a33-35 only defines the necessary as what cannot be otherwise (τὸ μὴ ἐνδεχόμενον ἄλλως ἔχειν ἀναγκαῖόν φαμεν οὕτως ἔχειν), and 1015b11-13 argues the converse of the bridge (the simple cannot be in more ways, so not otherwise and otherwise, since being otherwise and otherwise would already be being in more ways); so candidate ARIST-MET-V-5-NECESSARY-CANNOT-BE-OTHERWISE is exhausted without an Aristotle claim and is removed. Aquinas, V lect. 6 n. 14 states the needed direction: 'quae autem pluribus modis habere se possunt, possunt se habere aliter et aliter'. Claim AQUINAS-IN-METAPH-V-L6-MORE-WAYS-OTHERWISE-A reads it as STMT-WHAT-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-CAN-BE-OTHERWISE, through two stated reading choices: the two-way potency to r (able to be r and able not to be r) is an ability to be in two ways in r, and the respect of being otherwise is r. Sibling -B (STMT-WHAT-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-CAN-BE-OTHERWISE-IN-SOME-RESPECT) keeps the sentence unrelativized and is too weak for the route. (2) Scope bridge, partly supported only. Met. XII.9, 1074b25-27 says the divine thought does not change its object (change would be for the worse and already a kind of motion); Aquinas, XII lect. 11 n. 8 says the first mover cannot pass from one object of understanding to another, because such passing is a kind of motion and the first mover is 'omnino immobile'. Claim AQUINAS-IN-METAPH-XII-L11-FIRST-MOVER-UNDERSTANDING-UNCHANGEABLE-A states that for the respect of understanding (STMT-FIRST-MOVER-CANNOT-CHANGE-WHAT-IT-UNDERSTANDS, DEF-RESPECT-OF-WHAT-IS-UNDERSTOOD), and a supports relation records it as partial evidence for the scope bridge (some mover, moved in no respect at all, cannot be otherwise in understanding); the residue (that it cannot be otherwise in any further respect, in particular willing, and the universal form) stays unattributed and the bridge's paraphrase says so. (3) Rejected, with reasons: (a) reading Lambda.7's 'in no way' over every respect through 1072b13 (τὸ μὴ ἐνδεχόμενον ἄλλως ἀλλʼ ἁπλῶς, which Ross renders 'can exist only in a single way', i.e. V.5's simple): Aquinas, lect. 7 n. 13-15 refers the necessity of 1072b10-13 to the first motion and denies it is the absolute 'cannot be otherwise', so the reading is contested and was not adopted as a claim; (b) V lect. 6 n. 14's 'primum necessarium ... omnibus modis necessarium ... non aliter et aliter se habeat' for the scope bridge: it is said of the first necessary, and no text read identifies the first necessary with the Lambda.7 mover, so using it would add a bridge (the same leaf count); (c) splitting the scope bridge into the lect. 11 n. 8 reading plus a narrower residue: it would add a leaf to the route without reducing the bare residue's content, so the bridge is kept whole with a supports relation; (d) a reading of IX.8 straight to 'can be otherwise' merging the can-fail bridge with the potency of the contradictory: it would identify the two predicates silently, which DISAMB-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-OR-BE-OTHERWISE forbids; (e) Met. IX.8, 1050b18 (nothing that is of necessity is in potency) with 1072b10 (ἐξ ἀνάγκης ἄρα ἐστὶν ὄν): IX.8 says it with the qualification 'simply' (in substance), so it gives no potency in substance only; (f) lect. 7 n. 13 ('nullo modo potest moveri ... et sic non potest aliter et aliter se habere') with lect. 11 n. 8 ('omnino immobile') as a schema 'cannot be moved in r, so cannot be otherwise in r' plus 'immovable in every respect': it would need the modal 'immobile', which the case's MovedIn (actual) does not express, a new primitive and two premises in place of the one bridge, so it was not formalized; it is the next candidate source if a modal movability predicate is introduced; (g) lect. 8 n. 11 (primum movens, quod est in actu tantum) and 1072b27 (ἐκεῖνος δὲ ἡ ἐνέργεια): not recorded as stating claims, pending the owner question on #352. Recomposition: the argument, its Lean doc comments and the definition and disambiguation records now cite lect. 6 n. 14 for the can-fail bridge and lect. 11 n. 8 as partial support for the scope bridge; no premise or Lean type changed. Frontier: --routes unchanged (skeleton 31, cheapest); --reaching-root unchanged (63 open: 12 bare, 51 sourced), because the Lambda.7 derivation is not the selected one; the full frontier goes from 76 to 74 bare (both bridges become sourced). What-if without the ST I q.3 a.1 derivation: skeleton 32, unchanged from #584, since sourcing does not change leaf counts.
blocker: The Lambda.7 route cannot tie the ST I q.3 a.1 route on the sources read. It has four open leaves beside the already-paid uniqueness (the Lambda.7 reading, the scope bridge, the can-fail bridge, the potency of the contradictory) against q.3 a.1's three, and sourcing a leaf does not remove it. A tie needs one leaf fewer: a reading of 'in no way' over every respect that replaces both STMT-SOME-UNMOVED-MOVER-CANNOT-BE-OTHERWISE and the scope bridge (rejected above: (a), (b)), or one source that takes potency to 'can be otherwise' directly (none found; (d)). Beating it needs both. Next: look for a text that says the first mover cannot be otherwise in willing (for example ST I q.9 a.1 or q.19 a.7 on the immutability of God's will), and check (not read for this attempt; orientation only) whether ST I q.19 a.3 (God wills creatures not by absolute necessity) makes the scope bridge false over willing under the V lect. 6 sense of 'cannot be otherwise'; or settle the owner question on lect. 8 n. 11.
